sara.m: Ran the eval suite on the new 8-bit quant variant and hitting nondeterministic continuations even with the same seed. same prompt + --seed 42, different run -> different tokens after step 4. anyone seen this pattern?

kevin: Did you pin the seed at both process and worker level? we've had issues where worker reparenting resets per-worker seeds.

liam: can you paste the exact command + minimal logs?

sara.m: ```
./eval-runner --model qgpt-8bit --batch 1 --seed 42 --temperature 1.0 --top_p 0.9 --prompts prompts.jsonl
```
Observations: run A vs run B differ starting at token 5. checksum of first 64 tokens mismatches.

kevin: that CLI sets only the global RNG. runner spawns workers and historically some code did `srand(time(NULL))` in worker_start(). grep for srand in runner.

sara.m: I checked. global path seeds workers with seed+worker_id, but quant exec path calls into device init that does its own cuRAND setup using clock fallback if no seed is passed. so we have host sampler RNG + device cuRAND RNG -> potential divergence.

liam: Curand usage in quant kernels? why would it run for sampling?

kevin: we use curand for a few kernels (dropout-ish noise and some quant noise annealing) — recent perf changes created per-stream generators which may be ordered differently across runs. if streams interleave, ordering of draws changes.

sara.m: quick test: set curand seed explicitly and cudaStreamSynchronize before sampling reduced flakiness but didn't fully eliminate it.

liam: another angle: top_p selection comparator differences. quant softmax (int8->float) can produce tiny fp deltas and our cumsum comparator (<= vs <) can pick different indices.

kevin: good call. we had a known epsilon off-by-one in sampler: some implementations use `r <= cumsum` others `r < cumsum`. across implementations and fp rounding those can flip. make the comparator stable: `r < cumsum - 1e-8` or use deterministic tie-breaker.

sara.m: tentative fix plan: 1) wire device curand to the global seed (base_seed + worker_id) via curandSetPseudoRandomGeneratorSeed 2) enforce single-stream sampling when --force-single-stream 3) change sampler comparator to a stable epsilon 4) add a CI stability test that repeats fixed-seed runs 10x and asserts exact match.

kevin: for (1) also set curandSetGeneratorOrdering to CURAND_ORDERING_PSEUDO_DEFAULT and ensure we create generators deterministically per worker id. remember async memcpy can still reorder draws.

liam: for CI, first run cpu-only baseline to confirm quant/device path is the culprit, then add deterministic-quant job. keep the cpu run cheap.

sara.m: agreed. cpu-only runs are stable in my quick runs -> points strongly to device/quant path. will add a small repro harness and a `--dump-seeds` flag to log host_seed/device_seed/worker_id/curand_gen_id to make triage easier.

kevin: please also log sampler internal state: cumulative probs and threshold value for the sampled index so we can diff runs.

eval-bot: CI job eval/sampler-stability started for PR #2148 — cpu-only 10 repeats.

liam: small follow-up: check inclusive vs exclusive prefix sum implementation in quant softmax kernel. quant conversion order (dequantize->softmax vs fused approximations) can change rounding.

sara.m: will open a tiny PR with these three changes (seed wiring + comparator + dump flags) and add the CI flakiness test. ping me if you want to pair on curand wiring.

kevin: I'll pair tomorrow morning on the curand patch.

sara.m: thanks folks :thumbsup:
